headline: Poundland collapses into administration, 11,000 jobs at risk
pages: UK discount retailer Poundland has entered administration, putting 11,000 jobs at risk, after its owners failed to find a buyer. Stores and distribution centers will keep trading during the process, but the business is likely to be broken up with some stores sold to rivals. Its US owner, Gordon Brothers, held talks with several bidders on a last-minute rescue, but no deal was reached. CEO Barry Williams told staff the board had no alternative. He said the owner removed all borrowing facilities and access to bank accounts on October 27 and did not release enough funds afterward. A longtime employee told the BBC he feared he would not find another job at his age.
Alix Partners has been named to handle the administration. Source: BBC News.
